newsitem.title: CHINA: World Bank to loan China $3.0 bln in fiscal '97.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to loan China $3.0 bln in fiscal '97.

text.p: The World Bank will extend about $3.0 billion in loans to China in the fiscal year starting from July 1997, the Economic Daily on Tuesday quoted a bank official as saying.

The loans would be used to support China's market-oriented economic reforms, infrastructure projects and agriculture, the newspaper quoted Pieter Bottelier, World Bank chief of mission in China, as saying.
Poverty relief work would also be a focus of the bank's activities in China, Bottelier said but gave no details.
Bottelier could not be reached immediately to comment.
The bank's committee of donor nations had decided not to extend soft loans to China after the year 2000 but would use mixed loans and syndicated loans after that time, he said.
The World Bank would also continue to advise China on its modernisation drive, he said.
The bank had given out 175 loans to China totalling $26.0 billion since 1981, he said.
